question.text: The integral <math><mi>I</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">∫</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mrow><mi>e</mi></mrow><mrow><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></mrow></msup><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">cos</mi></mrow><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msup><mrow><mi>e</mi></mrow><mrow><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced></mrow></mrow></mrow><mrow><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></math><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mi>x</mi></mfenced><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></math> (where, <math><mi>c</mi></math> is the constant of integration) and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><msup><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mfenced separators="|"><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mfenced></mrow></mfenced><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>.</mo></math> Then, the number of solutions of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mi>x</mi></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>e</mi><mo> </mo><mfenced><mrow><mo>∀</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>-</mo><mfenced close="}" open="{" separators="|"><mn>0</mn></mfenced></mrow></mfenced></math> is equal to

solution.text:
Given integral is
I=∫excos⁡exxdx
Let ex=t
⇒ex2xdx=dt
∴I=2∫cos⁡tdt
=2sin⁡t+c
=2sin⁡ex+c
∴fx=2sin⁡ex
which has range =-2,2
Hence, fx=2e has no solution
